record.original_question: Is the subgroup ⟨PSL(2)(k) , PSL(2)(l) ⟩ in Diff ω (S1 ) isomorphic to the amalgamated product PSL(2)(k) ∗SO(2) PSL(2)(l) ?

evidence.quote: Question 8.6. Is the subgroup ⟨PSL(2)(k) , PSL(2)(l) ⟩ in Diff ω (S1 ) isomorphic to the amalgamated product PSL(2)(k) ∗SO(2) PSL(2)(l) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1 = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ and let $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(S^1)$ denote the group of real-analytic orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of $S^1$. The standard projective action of $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ on $S^1 \cong \mathbb{RP}^1$ embeds $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ as a subgroup of $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(S^1)$, with rotation subgroup $\mathrm{SO}(2) \subset \mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ acting as the standard rotations.

For each positive integer $k \ge 1$, the $k$-fold cyclic cover $S^1 \to S^1$, $x \mapsto kx$, allows one to lift the $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$-action to a faithful real-analytic action on $S^1$; equivalently, one obtains an injective homomorphism
$$
\mathrm{PSL}^{(k)}(2,\mathbb{R}) \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(S^1),
$$
where $\mathrm{PSL}^{(k)}(2,\mathbb{R})$ denotes the connected $k$-fold cover of $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. Under this embedding, the maximal compact subgroup $\mathrm{SO}(2) \subset \mathrm{PSL}^{(k)}(2,\mathbb{R})$ is sent to the rigid rotations of $S^1$, and this rotation subgroup is the same $\mathrm{SO}(2) \subset \mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(S^1)$ for every $k$.

Fix two distinct positive integers $k \neq l$, and consider the subgroup
$$
G_{k,l} \;=\; \bigl\langle \mathrm{PSL}^{(k)}(2,\mathbb{R}),\; \mathrm{PSL}^{(l)}(2,\mathbb{R}) \bigr\rangle \;\subset\; \mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(S^1)
$$
generated (inside $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(S^1)$) by the images of these two embeddings, which intersect along the common rotation subgroup $\mathrm{SO}(2)$.

Question. Is $G_{k,l}$ isomorphic, via the natural map, to the amalgamated free product
$$
\mathrm{PSL}^{(k)}(2,\mathbb{R}) \;*_{\mathrm{SO}(2)}\; \mathrm{PSL}^{(l)}(2,\mathbb{R}) \,?
$$
